observation_summary: The SerializationUtils.clone method uses a custom ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream that overrides resolveClass. This override attempts to load classes using two different class loaders but fails to fall back to the default ObjectInputStream.resolveClass implementation, which is required to handle primitive types (e.g., 'int.class') correctly.
hypothesis: The ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream.resolveClass method fails to resolve primitive classes because it does not delegate to the super.resolveClass() method, which contains the necessary logic to handle primitive type names (e.g., 'int', 'boolean') as defined in the Java ObjectInputStream specification.
prediction: If I modify the resolveClass method in ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream to call super.resolveClass(desc) when both Class.forName attempts fail, the primitive classes will be correctly resolved.
experiment_rationale: The bug report explicitly identifies the missing delegation to super.resolveClass() as the cause of the failure to resolve primitive classes, which is a known behavior of the standard ObjectInputStream. The fix is a procedural change to the resolution logic.
reasoning_summary: The failure occurs because the custom resolveClass implementation in SerializationUtils does not handle primitive types. The standard Java ObjectInputStream.resolveClass handles these types internally. By failing to call super.resolveClass(), the custom implementation loses this capability. This is a procedural error in the implementation of the class resolution algorithm.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves adding a check/fallback, the root cause is the incorrect implementation of the class resolution procedure, which is better classified as an Algorithm/Method issue.
